missing_supported_requirements.why_missing: The draft states the objective (effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital over short/medium/long term) but does not actually disclose information about all sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects; it focuses on climate examples only and does not evidence completeness across sustainability topics.

No explicit statement that additional information is provided when specifically applicable IFRS SDS requirements are insufficient, nor a clear explanation of how the entity assessed sufficiency and supplemented disclosures accordingly.

The draft states the reporting year and fiscal year end but does not explicitly state that the sustainability-related financial disclosures are for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements (eg, same consolidation perimeter).

The draft provides some financial-statement-type figures (Tier 1 capital, capex) but does not explain connections across sustainability disclosures and other general purpose financial reports (eg, where in the financial statements related items are presented, or how figures reconcile/align).
The draft does not identify the specific financial statements to which the sustainability-related financial disclosures relate (eg, consolidated financial statements for year ended 31 Dec 2024).

The draft includes emissions data-quality sourcing but does not address consistency of data and assumptions with those used in the related financial statements (eg, alignment of capex definitions, consolidation scope, measurement bases) to the extent possible.

The draft states EUR is used when currency is the unit of measure, but does not explicitly state that EUR is the presentation currency of the related financial statements (as required when currency is specified).

No disclosure that the entity referred to and considered the applicability of SASB disclosure topics (or concluded they are not applicable). The sovereign bonds methodological note is not a SASB consideration statement.

The draft does not state that, for each sustainability-related risk/opportunity, it applied the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard that specifically applies (eg, IFRS S2 for climate) as the basis for identifying applicable disclosure requirements.
No explicit disclosure describing the judgement process used when no specific IFRS SDS applies, nor how the selected information is relevant to users’ decision-making in those cases.

No explicit disclosure describing how the judgement-based information faithfully represents the risk/opportunity when no specific IFRS SDS applies (eg, completeness/neutrality/accuracy considerations for those items).
No disclosure that the entity referred to and considered SASB metrics when making the paragraph 57 judgement (or concluded they are not applicable).

The draft does not identify the specific standards/pronouncements/industry practice and other guidance applied in preparing the sustainability-related financial disclosures (eg, IFRS S1/S2, GHG Protocol, PCAF), nor any SASB topics if applicable.
The draft does not identify the industry/industries (per IFRS SDS/SASB/other guidance) applied in preparing disclosures and identifying applicable metrics (eg, commercial banks).
The draft does not describe any use of cross-references to other reports, nor does it apply the cross-reference requirements (location, availability, same terms, etc.).
The draft states the reporting period covered but does not state that sustainability disclosures are reported at the same time as the related financial statements.

snippets: issuer EVIC (EUR million) and issuer revenue (EUR million) are null for sovereign bonds by design

required_fixes: Remove or rephrase the 'null' wording about sovereign bond EVIC/revenue so it does not present missing/unavailable data in the report text (policy). If needed, describe the methodological boundary without using missing-data language (eg, 'EVIC and revenue are not applicable measures for sovereigns and are therefore not used in the calculation').

Add an explicit identification of the related financial statements (eg, 'These sustainability-related financial disclosures relate to the consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024').
Add an explicit statement that the sustainability disclosures are for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements (same consolidation perimeter).
Add an explicit statement that the presentation currency used for currency-denominated sustainability information is the presentation currency of the related financial statements.
Add a brief description of connectivity across sustainability disclosures and the financial statements/other GPFR (eg, where referenced financial figures come from, and/or reconciliation/links).

Add disclosures identifying the specific standards/guidance applied (eg, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, GHG Protocol, PCAF, NGFS/IEA inputs) and the industry classification used; include the required SASB consideration statements (topics/metrics considered or not applicable).

If claiming completeness per IFRS S1.3, either broaden beyond climate to 'all sustainability-related risks and opportunities' or scope the section clearly as climate-only and ensure the overall report elsewhere covers all sustainability-related risks/opportunities.
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: Not approved due to (1) prohibited missing-data language ('null') and (2) multiple supported IFRS S1 general requirements not yet explicitly addressed (link to financial statements/reporting entity, presentation currency linkage, SASB consideration and sources of guidance, cross-report connectivity, and timing statement). The section is strong on climate examples, comparatives, and internal connectivity across governance/strategy/risk/metrics, but it does not yet meet several explicit general-requirement disclosures.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: The disclosures are prepared for the reporting year 2024, with a financial year end of 31 December 2024, and are presented in EUR when currency is used as the unit of measure. Comparative information is presented for 2022 and 2023...
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Reporting year, year-end, currency, and comparative years are supported by evidence_items (metadata.reporting_year, bank.fiscal_year_end, bank.reporting_currency, metadata.comparative_years). However, the statement is bundled with broader assertions about how comparatives are presented 'alongside the current reporting year where amounts are disclosed across periods' without showing the full set of disclosures or a policy note; only selected examples are evidenced.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: For 2024, operational greenhouse gas emissions are disclosed as Scope 1... Scope 2... Scope 3 (business travel)... Financed emissions are disclosed for 2024 as 35,973,167.6878965 tCO₂e, and a portfolio carbon intensity metric... 1,154.8131 tCO₂e per EUR million.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: No evidence_items provided for operational Scope 1/2/3 values or for the 2024 financed emissions and portfolio carbon intensity values. The only related evidence_item is financial_summary[0].financed_em_loans_tco2e for 2022 (and it differs from the draft’s 2024 financed emissions figure).

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Scope 2 market-based emissions are sourced directly from utility invoices and already reflect market-based accounting with grid emission factors adjusted for renewable energy certificates and power purchase agreements...
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: No evidence_items (e.g., methodology documentation, invoice-based sourcing controls, REC/PPA treatment) are provided to substantiate this specific sourcing and adjustment approach.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: The disclosures include indicators of physical risk exposure classification... high-risk flags are True for five of the eight listed physical risk exposure entries.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: No evidence_items include the referenced list of eight entries or the five 'True' flags; therefore the count cannot be verified.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: The bank discloses green loans as 10.71% (2024)...
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: No evidence_items provided for the 10.71% figure or its definition/denominator.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Targets are disclosed... target TGT001... progress in 2024 of 40.0%... intensity progress 25.0%... percentage reduction... 13.3%.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: No evidence_items provided for target TGT001 attributes or progress metrics.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Under disorderly transition scenarios, the bank’s scenario analysis indicates higher transition-risk impacts than under orderly pathways...
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Evidence_items include disorderly and orderly resilience_assessment narratives, but they do not explicitly state a comparative conclusion 'higher than orderly' in a way that can be verified from provided evidence; it is an inference.

unsupported_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Under orderly transition scenarios... Transition risk losses remain within Pillar 2 capital buffer thresholds.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Evidence_items include this sentence in climate_scenarios[0/1/2/3/4/5].resilience_assessment, but no quantitative thresholds, calculations, or references are provided to substantiate 'remain within'.

questionable_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Climate-related capital expenditure is presented on a consistent basis across the three-year period...
questionable_claims.why_questionable: The numeric values are supported by financial_summary climate_capex_meur for 2022–2024, but 'consistent basis' implies a stable definition/methodology across years; no evidence of unchanged definition or restatements is provided.

questionable_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Tier 1 capital is also presented across the same comparative years...
questionable_claims.why_questionable: The numeric values are supported by financial_summary tier1_capital_meur for 2022–2024, but there is no linkage to audited financial statements or reconciliation in evidence_items.

questionable_claims.claim_or_excerpt: Connected information enables users to understand how governance oversight, strategic responses, risk management processes, and performance metrics relate...
questionable_claims.why_questionable: This is a qualitative assertion about usefulness; not directly verifiable from provided evidence.

required_fixes: Add evidence (data table extracts or referenced source IDs) for 2024 operational emissions (Scope 1, Scope 2 location-based, Scope 2 market-based, Scope 3 business travel).

Add evidence for 2024 financed emissions and 2024 portfolio carbon intensity, including boundary (which portfolios), methodology (e.g., PCAF), and reconciliation to any underlying dataset; resolve the apparent mismatch with evidence showing 2022 financed emissions loans value.

Provide support for the Scope 2 market-based sourcing/treatment claim (e.g., documented methodology note, control description, or audit/assurance reference) showing invoices/contractual instruments and how RECs/PPAs are reflected.
Provide the underlying list for the 'five of eight high-risk flags' physical risk exposure classification or remove/soften the quantified count.
Provide evidence and definition for 'green loans 10.71% (2024)' (taxonomy/criteria, numerator/denominator, scope).
Provide evidence for target TGT001 and progress metrics (baseline value, target end date, calculation of progress percentages, and scope).

If keeping comparative statements about disorderly vs orderly impacts and Pillar 2 buffer compliance, add quantified results or explicit comparative statements from the scenario outputs; otherwise rephrase as qualitative narrative without comparative/threshold assertions.
evidence_judge.summary: Several governance, risk-register, and scenario-methodology statements are supported by provided evidence_items (e.g., risk register excerpts, governance metrics, scenario methodology notes, capex and Tier 1 values). However, key quantitative climate metrics (operational emissions, 2024 financed emissions, portfolio carbon intensity), green loan percentage, target progress metrics, and the physical-risk '5 of 8' count lack supporting evidence in the supplied evidence_items. Some scenario resilience statements are present as narrative evidence but remain weakly supported without underlying calculations or thresholds.

voice_issues: Section uses neutral, standards-aligned voice overall, but does not consistently distinguish between current-period facts, estimates, and forward-looking intentions (e.g., scenario analysis narratives read as factual without explicit modality such as 'could' or 'is expected to').

Point of view is mostly third-person ('the bank'), which is acceptable, but the section_style guidance prefers an explicit, consistent choice and clearer accountability phrasing (e.g., 'we prepare', 'we disclose') for basis-of-preparation statements.

Some phrasing is more explanatory than assurance-like (e.g., 'This section explains how...') and could be tightened to a more formal disclosure voice ('This section describes the basis of preparation...').
structure_issues: Headings are not numbered and do not follow the requested two-level hierarchy aligned to IFRS S1/S2 (e.g., 1, 1.1, 1.2). Current headings are free-form ('Basis of preparation, reporting period, currency and comparatives', 'Connected information across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics').

The section does not start with a concise, explicit basis-of-preparation statement followed by a bulleted list of qualitative characteristics and preparation principles, as required by the section_style.
Paragraphs often combine multiple ideas (e.g., scenario methodology, scope, and impacts in one block) rather than keeping single-idea, topic-led paragraphs.

The layered structure rule (overview → structured bullets/tables → brief interpretation and cross-references) is only partially followed; there are few bullets and no tables, and cross-references to other sections are largely absent.

IFRS pillar subheadings (Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics and Targets) are not used explicitly; instead, 'Connected information' is used with embedded bold labels, which is less scannable and not aligned to the prescribed structure.

Major subsections do not consistently close with a short connectivity sentence linking to related sections or financial statements using the specified cross-reference placeholders (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance]').
wording_issues: The section includes many specific numeric values (years, amounts, percentages) even though the section_style explicitly instructs to avoid hard-coding reporting years, dates, currencies, and performance claims in this general requirements template section.

Some sentences are long and multi-clause, reducing clarity and not fully aligned with the short-to-medium sentence preference (e.g., scenario methodology descriptions and risk transmission mechanisms).

Forward-looking and scenario-related content sometimes lacks cautious modality; impacts are described as if certain rather than as potential outcomes ('the bank assesses portfolio resilience' without clarifying that results are model-based estimates).
The section occasionally blends 'what' and 'how' in the same paragraph (e.g., risk rating methodology paragraphs mix principles and mechanics) instead of clearly separating them.

Terminology is mostly consistent but could more explicitly use controlled vocabulary such as 'sustainability-related risks and opportunities' vs 'climate-related risks and opportunities' when appropriate, and more clearly distinguish current-period facts from estimates and forward-looking intentions.
table_figure_issues: No tables or figures are used, even where compact tables could improve scanability (e.g., summarising reporting period, currency, comparatives, or mapping connected information to IFRS pillars).

Because there are no tables or figures, there are no captions or references; this is acceptable but does not fully leverage the style guidance that encourages simple tables for basis-of-preparation mappings.
required_fixes: Restructure headings to follow the required numbered hierarchy and IFRS pillar alignment. For example, use '1. General requirements', '1.1 Basis of preparation and reporting boundary', '1.2 Connected information', '1.3 Comparatives and consistency', and ensure explicit subheadings for Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets where relevant.

Introduce an opening basis-of-preparation paragraph that clearly states the scope, reporting boundary, and standards alignment, followed by a bulleted list of key preparation principles and qualitative characteristics (e.g., completeness, neutrality, accuracy, use of estimates).

Remove or generalise hard-coded reporting years, dates, currencies, and specific numeric performance values in this general requirements template section, or clearly frame them as example placeholders if this is intended as a reusable template. Align with the 'what_to_avoid' list by not embedding fixed years, amounts, or percentages in the generic basis-of-preparation narrative.

Shorten and split long, multi-clause sentences, especially in the scenario analysis and risk description paragraphs, to improve clarity and align with the short-to-medium sentence guidance. Ensure each sentence has a clear subject–verb–object structure.

Clarify the distinction between current-period facts, estimates/judgements, and forward-looking information. For scenario analysis and resilience narratives, explicitly state that results are model-based estimates and use cautious modality ('could', 'may', 'is expected to') rather than definitive language.

Increase use of bullets for lists of risks, methodologies, and data-quality characteristics to better follow the layered structure rule. For example, present the climate risk register examples and data-quality distributions as structured bullet lists with parallel grammar.

Add brief closing connectivity sentences at the end of major subsections, using the prescribed cross-reference style (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance] for further detail on board oversight of climate-related risks.').

Consider adding at least one compact table to summarise key basis-of-preparation elements (e.g., reporting boundary, period, currency, comparatives, value chain coverage) with a clear caption and narrative reference, in line with the table_usage guidance.

Ensure the voice is consistently formal and assurance-like. Replace conversational lead-ins such as 'This section explains how...' with more formal formulations such as 'This section describes the basis of preparation for the sustainability-related financial disclosures.'
style_judge.summary: The section is technically detailed, neutral, and largely aligned with an IFRS-style disclosure voice, but it does not fully comply with the approved authoring style. Key gaps include lack of numbered, IFRS-aligned headings; absence of an explicit basis-of-preparation principles list; overuse of hard-coded years and numeric values in what should be a reusable general requirements template; and some long, multi-topic sentences. With structural adjustments, clearer separation of facts vs estimates vs forward-looking information, and removal or generalisation of fixed period- and amount-specific content, the section could be brought into full compliance.
